newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.AFRICAN OPPOSITION COMPLAIN OVER DRUGS BILL.
newsitem.headline: S.AFRICAN OPPOSITION COMPLAIN OVER DRUGS BILL.

text.p: South Africa's five main opposition parties found rare common ground on Monday, joining in a protest at what they called government attempts to push through controversial legislation on pharmaceuticals.

Drug manufacturers have threatened to go to court to block three bills, introduced in parliament by Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma last week, saying the legislation amounts to nationalisation of the industry.

The Democratic Party, the Inkatha Freedom Party, the Freedom Front, the National Party and the Pan Africanist Congress signed a joint statement saying they "strongly opposed attempts by the government to push (the bills) through parliament before the end of the present session".
"These are major bills with far-reaching implications for the sale of pharmaceuticals and the roles of the medical and dental council and pharmaceutical council," a joint statement said.

"If adequate time for public debate and wide consultation on these bills is not provided for, the passage will represent a mockery of the so-called transparent and consultative paliamentary process," the statement said.
The Democratic Party said in a separate statement that the health ministry had allowed for only one morning of discussion in a parliamentary committee for each bill.
